reference_diagnosis.name: GLUT1 deficiency syndrome (SLC2A1) with paroxysmal exercise-induced dyskinesia
reference_diagnosis.basis: Early-onset absence epilepsy (<4 years), paroxysmal exertion-induced dyskinesia worse with fasting, mild cognitive impairment and ataxia, low CSF glucose with low CSF:blood ratio, SLC2A1 variant, response to ketogenic diet.

competing_hypotheses.what_argues_against: Early onset <4 y and exertion-induced dystonia/chorea are a recognized combination; fasting link
PKD attacks are seconds long, triggered by sudden movement, not prolonged exertion
Normal lactate, normal MRI; less specific

competing_hypotheses.why_plausible: Childhood leg dystonia worse with exertion
competing_hypotheses.what_argues_against: Episodes are discrete with full recovery after rest, linked to fasting and helped by sugar; early absence epilepsy, ataxia and learning difficulty are not explained by DRD

key_evidence_gaps.question: Paired fasting CSF and blood glucose
key_evidence_gaps.why_it_matters: CSF:blood ratio is the key test

held_out_evidence.investigation: Lumbar puncture after 4–6 h fast with paired blood glucose
held_out_evidence.result: CSF glucose 1.9 mmol/L, blood 4.6 mmol/L, ratio 0.41; CSF lactate low-normal.
Heterozygous de novo pathogenic SLC2A1 variant.
Marked reduction of exercise-induced episodes and absences at 3 months.

discriminating_investigations.investigation: Fasting LP with paired blood glucose
Attack phenomenology and trigger (prolonged exertion vs. sudden movement)

cant_miss.why_required: Treatable: ketogenic diet; early-onset absence epilepsy (before 4) plus exercise-induced dyskinesia should prompt testing
cant_miss.addressed_by: Fasting lumbar puncture with paired blood glucose; SLC2A1 genetics
Clinical pattern; levodopa trial if GLUT1 is excluded
cant_miss.status_in_record: considered, unlikely: paroxysmal with fasting link and seizures

cant_miss.why_required: Treatable; considered in any unexplained movement disorder, most strongly under 50
cant_miss.status_in_record: low risk: age 10, liver tests normal, paroxysmal pattern

red_flags_for_wrong_reasoning: Treating the epilepsy and movement episodes as unrelated without considering a unifying diagnosis
Interpreting CSF glucose without a paired blood glucose
Calling a normal fasting blood glucose evidence against GLUT1DS
Stating any diagnosis as established rather than as a hypothesis for physician review
Recommending treatment as an instruction rather than a consideration for the treating physician
Citing literature that does not exist or does not support the specific claim
Asserting case facts that are not in the case record
Overlooking that valproate, previously used, can worsen GLUT1 deficiency (relevant history, not a treatment instruction)
clinician_review_notes: Clinical review 2026-10-17 (pending Wiki sign-off). Classic GLUT1 deficiency. Added DRD as a hypothesis and to the acceptable top 5 (childhood exercise-induced leg dystonia must prompt it under the reasoning rules), cant_miss, one red flag and expected behaviour.
expected_system_behavior: GLUT1 deficiency should rank first as a unifying diagnosis for early-onset absence epilepsy, exercise-induced leg dyskinesia worse when fasting, mild ataxia and learning difficulty. The system should reject 'two unrelated conditions', separate PED from PKD by trigger, consider DRD and downgrade it, and suggest a fasting lumbar puncture with paired blood glucose and SLC2A1 testing.
